title: Eleven Witnesses and One Lane
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：crime　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 crime 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 my grandmother ① witnessed a crime in a lane that had eleven doors on it, and she said the witnessing was the whole of the statement. The ② crime, meaning the act and not the trial, took eleven seconds and stayed that short; crime, she said, is the only thing in a lane that is judged by how many doors stay shut.

Every ③ crime in that town had the same witness, and the ④ crime at the end, meaning the one she kept from the police and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever described twice. Crime, my mother said, is nine parts witness and one part somebody willing to speak; my grandmother said the speaking is the part that fills eleven seconds.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the crime was the whole of the report, meaning the wrong of it and not the act. The ⑥ crime, meaning the wrong and not any of that, is the only thing in a report that everybody agrees about and nobody defines; crime, he said, is either something you witness or the only word that means both an act and a wrong. She said the wrong is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ crime had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the witness. The ⑧ crime of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in March, was one lane and thirty years of speaking; crime, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to speak. He said the speaking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ crime I remember is the one at the end, which was reported in 1971 and is still described as the shortest in the county. A ⑩ crime, my mother said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being spoken of; every crime, she said, is a wrong that has agreed to look like an act. She said the wrong was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 罪行（指那件行为本身，与那场审判相对）
C. 固定搭配：witness a crime 目击一起犯罪
D. n. 案件（指那个镇上每一起）
E. n. 案件（指末尾那一起）
F. n. 不法；罪过（抽象：事情本身的不正当）
G. n. 案件（指登记簿上提到的那一起）
H. n. 犯罪活动（抽象总称）

items.q: witnessed a crime in a lane that had eleven doors on it
The crime, meaning the act and not the trial
the crime was the whole of the report
the crime had become a line in a register
The crime of the whole thing
A crime, my mother said in 1973

answers.why: witness a crime 意为“目击一起犯罪”，1957 年祖母在一条有十一扇门的小巷里目击了一起犯罪。
crime 意为“罪行”，指那件行为本身而不是那场审判，只用了十一秒。
crime 指那个镇上每一起案件，每一起都有同一个目击者。
crime 指末尾那一起（她对警方隐瞒的那一起），是唯一有人描述过两次的。
crime 意为“不法、罪过”，父亲说那份不正当就是那份报告的全部，指的是事情本身的不正当而不是那件行为。
crime 为抽象用法，指事情本身的不正当而不是那件行为，是报告里人人都认同、却无人下定义的东西。
crime 意为“案件”，指登记簿上提到的那一起，到 1965 年这起案件成了登记簿里的一行。
crime 意为“犯罪活动”，祖母三月写道，整件事的犯罪活动是一条小巷三十年的开口。
crime 意为“罪行、犯罪”，我记得的是末尾那一起，1971 年报案，至今仍被说成全县最短的。
crime 为抽象总称，母亲说一起犯罪是唯一会因为被说出来而变好的东西。

那件罪行，指的是那件行为本身而不是那场审判，只用了十一秒，并且一直是那么短。（crime）
那个镇上每一起案件都有同一个目击者。（crime）
末尾那一起案件，指的是她对警方隐瞒的那一起，是唯一有人描述过两次的。（crime）
父亲说那份不正当就是那份报告的全部，指的是事情本身的不正当而不是那件行为。（crime）

answers: In 1957 my grandmother witnessed a crime in a lane that had eleven doors on it, and she said the witnessing was the whole of the statement.
The crime, meaning the act and not the trial, took eleven seconds and stayed that short.
Every crime in that town had the same witness.
The crime at the end, meaning the one she kept from the police and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever described twice.
My father said the crime was the whole of the report, meaning the wrong of it and not the act.
A crime, my mother said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being spoken of.
